newsitem.title: USA: US could rule on ValuJet this week-report.
newsitem.headline: US could rule on ValuJet this week-report.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) could issue a final ruling on ValuJet Inc's resumption of flight service by the end of this week, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported on Thursday.
The newspaper quoted an aide to U.S. Rep. Mac Collins of Georgia as saying that this week was "looking good" for a final ruling from the government.
ValuJet officials were not available for comment on the report.

ValuJet was forced to suspend operations in June amid a swarm of alleged safety violations discovered in the aftermath of the May 11 crash of Flight 592 in the Florida Everglades, which left 110 people dead.

The DOT tentatively appoved ValuJet's restart on August 29, the same day the Federal Aviation Administration returned the airline's operating certificate. The department then allowed 11 days for objections and company responses and has spent the last two weeks in review.

The Association of Flight Attendants, some relatives of Flight 592 victims and at least one stockholder have lodged objections, arguing that the airline should not be allowed to fly except with new top management.
The newspaper said DOT officials rejected that demand in their tentative approval but were obligated to consider any additional issues raised.
Earlier this week, ValuJet executives told employees that some of the 400 workers who have stayed with the company during its shutdown could face layoffs if approval did not come soon.
If a favorable ruling were to come this week, the newspaper said, ValuJet flights would be likely to start by the middle of next week.
